agentCan: Enable the Drive API, create the client, and declare scopes via Google Cloud APIs
Implement the Picker + drive.file flow, watch/changes sync, and download capability checks
Run the downscope analysis (which features truly need whole-Drive access) and draft justifications

approval.cost: Free; the CASA assessment for the restricted path is paid to a Google-approved assessor at an unpublished price
approval.trigger: Brand verification always. Beyond that it forks: the drive.file path needs only basic verification (Google advertises a streamlined process). Adding drive.apps.readonly (the one sensitive scope) triggers sensitive-scope verification (stated: typically 3-5 business days). Any restricted scope (whole-Drive read, metadata, activity, scripts) triggers restricted verification: a permitted-application-type defense plus an annual CASA security assessment if data is accessed from/through a server, re-certified every 12 months from the LOA date.
approval.wait: Basic (drive.file path): no separate stated duration. Sensitive: typically 3-5 business days. Restricted: potentially several weeks, plus assessment scheduling (all stated by Google)

blockers.detail: Searching or enumerating a user's whole Drive requires drive.readonly or drive, both restricted. That single product requirement buys restricted verification, a permitted-type defense (only backup/sync, productivity-and-education with a primary Drive-facing UI, or reporting/security qualify), and an annual CASA assessment for any server-side agent.
blockers.howToClear: Redesign around drive.file + Picker if you possibly can. If whole-Drive search is truly the product, budget the restricted path honestly and fit the productivity/education type.
blockers.title: Whole-Drive access triggers the full restricted apparatus

blockers.detail: With drive.file your app sees only files it created or files the user explicitly opened/shared with it via the Picker. files.list will not surface the rest of the user's Drive. An agent designed to 'browse everything' returns empty results by design.
blockers.howToClear: Build the UX around file picking (or app-created files) instead of browsing; say so in your onboarding copy.
blockers.title: The drive.file visibility model surprises agent builders

blockers.detail: Shared-drive items are invisible unless requests pass supportsAllDrives=true (and includeItemsFromAllDrives/corpora for search). An agent built and tested only against My Drive silently misses shared-drive content.
blockers.howToClear: Pass the shared-drive parameters from day one and test against a shared drive, not just My Drive.
blockers.title: Shared drives are opt-in per request

tested: Read-only verification: Drive's complete per-scope tier tables, the drive.file model, permitted application types for restricted scopes, export/download limits, and Picker rules were checked against current developers.google.com and support.google.com pages (no project created, nothing submitted)
unverified: CASA assessment cost and duration for Drive restricted scopes: not stated in the Drive docs read (Google publishes neither).
Hands-on time: Google quantifies only waiting times.
Whether a headless agent (no Drive-facing UI) cleanly fits the 'productivity and education' permitted type is an inference from Google's 'primary user interface' wording, not a Google statement.

flavor.recommended: A Google Cloud OAuth client requesting drive.file, with the Google Picker as the file-selection UX
flavor.why: Drive is the one Google API with a designed escape hatch: drive.file is non-sensitive, so the picker-based design (user picks exact files; you get full read/write on those files only) skips sensitive and restricted verification entirely. Google explicitly recommends this path and formally advises migrating restricted-scope apps to it. Every broader scope is a deliberate purchase of review burden.

humanMust: All Google platform human steps (login/2FA, ToS, Search Console domain proof, brand publish, demo video if verifying, reviewer replies)
Make the fork decision: picker-based design vs whole-Drive access
If restricted: fit a permitted application type and run the annual CASA cycle
name: Google Drive
nuances: Even metadata-only access is restricted: drive.metadata.readonly exposes no file content yet sits in the restricted tier, exactly like Gmail's metadata trap. There is no read-only-metadata middle tier.
Do not copy Google's own sample scope lists blindly: the Drive auth guide's samples pair drive.file with drive.metadata.readonly, which would silently move you into the restricted tier.

Exports of Google Workspace documents are capped at 10 MB of exported content; larger files need download/long-running-operation flows. Downloads are capability-gated (check capabilities.canDownload; owner-restricted and abusive-flagged files have special rules), and a metadata scope never authorizes downloading content.
On desktop/mobile, the Picker permits ONLY drive.file and it cannot be combined with other scopes; the web Picker is more flexible.

Google's reviewers actively downscope using a published ladder (drive -> drive.file/appdata/readonly; metadata -> metadata.readonly), with a reply protocol of 'Confirm Downscoping' vs 'Unable to use narrower scopes' plus explanation. Expect that email if you over-ask.
prerequisites: The Google platform setup from the Google guide (Cloud project, branding, verified domain, External audience, OAuth client)
The Drive API enabled in the project
A product design decision: Picker-based (drive.file) vs whole-Drive (restricted path)

steps.detail: Create the Cloud project, branding, External audience, and OAuth client exactly as in the Google guide, then enable the Drive API. No Drive-specific console exists.
steps.title: Set up the Google platform (see Google guide)

steps.detail: Default design: drive.file + Google Picker. The user picks the exact files; you get full read/write on just those. App-private storage: drive.appdata/appfolder instead of real files. Only choose whole-Drive scopes (drive.readonly/drive) if searching the user's entire Drive is genuinely the product, and accept the restricted path that comes with them.
steps.title: Design around drive.file first

steps.detail: Data Access page: declare exactly what your code requests. With only non-sensitive scopes (drive.file, appdata, install), verification stays basic and Google advertises a streamlined process. Adding drive.apps.readonly (the single sensitive scope) buys the 3-5 business day sensitive verification; any restricted scope buys the full path.
steps.title: Declare scopes matching your fork

steps.detail: Publish branding first. Basic path: branding verification only. Sensitive/restricted paths: submit with per-scope justifications and the demo video (English, full grant flow, correct app name, client ID in the address bar, each scope in use). Restricted path additionally: demonstrate a permitted application type (backup/sync; productivity and education with a primary Drive-file UI; reporting and security).
steps.time: Prep ~2 hrs; waiting per path (days to several weeks)
steps.title: Submit the verification your fork requires

steps.detail: Only on the restricted path with server-side data access: complete the CASA assessment with a Google-approved assessor after other verification steps, and calendar the annual re-certification (every 12 months from the LOA date; new restricted scopes may trigger reassessment).
steps.title: (Restricted path only) Complete CASA

steps.detail: Implement the Picker (web JS library, setOAuthToken), drive.file file operations, download checks (capabilities.canDownload, 10 MB export cap), shared-drive parameters (supportsAllDrives=true) if relevant, and files.watch/changes.watch channels with your own renewal (channels expire, no auto-renewal, empty notification bodies).
steps.title: Implement Picker, downloads, and change feeds

tagline: The Google API with an escape hatch: design around drive.file and the Picker and you skip the heavy verification entirely. Need to search a user's whole Drive and you buy the restricted tier, permitted-type defense, and annual security audit.

time.active: Platform setup ~1 hr (shared) + Picker integration ~half a day; restricted path adds justification and assessment prep
time.total: Days on the drive.file path; several weeks to months on the restricted path
time.waiting: Basic: brand verification only. Sensitive: typically 3-5 business days. Restricted: potentially several weeks plus assessment (stated)
